[cowork 20:15Z tick] signal_backlog has a PERMANENT FLOOR of 30 undrainable files, so signal_backlog_tier is pinned 'high' by construction and gatherer-standard's throttle-down cadence branches are unreachable.

WHAT signal_backlog IS: emitPressureStateTool.ts:510 defines it as 'docs/signals/*.json count excl cowork-team-*'. It is a FILE-drain backlog, NOT the orch-state .signal_queue NEW count (which was 0 this tick while the gauge read 38). Anyone reasoning about one from the other is wrong; the two queues are unrelated.

NATURAL EXPERIMENT (measured live, 2026-08-24): at 20:20Z the dir held 59 files (21 cowork-team-*) -> gauge 38. A peer drain ran between 20:20Z and 20:26Z. At 20:26Z: 48 files (18 cowork-team-*) -> 30. The drain took every file it could and left EXACTLY 30 -- and all 30 fail `has("from") and has("type")`, i.e. they are structurally undrainable. Drainable count after the sweep: 0.

THE 30: 22x price_anomaly_*.json (2026-07-02 .. 2026-08-24), 3x stranded-state-sweep-*, 2x cowork-signal-*, 2x dev-team-*, 1x cowork-tick-snapshot-regime-mismatch.

WHY IT IS PERMANENT AND GROWING: the drain skips them precisely BECAUSE they lack the envelope, but the gauge counts them regardless -- it is a raw file count. So a file that can never be drained is counted as drain-backlog forever. The price_anomaly emitter is still live (newest file is today, 20260824T1600), so the floor grows ~1 per trading day. Monotonically rising gauge with no path down.

CONSEQUENCE: computeTiers thresholds are 0-2=low, 3-9=medium, >=10=high (scripts/agents-flow/cadence-policy.js:79-82). Floor 30 is 3x the high threshold. Only gatherer-standard keys on this tier; its cal=open rules are backlog high->30min, medium->60min, low+vol_high->60min, low+vol_low->240min. The medium and low branches are therefore DEAD CODE -- unreachable regardless of how quiet the market actually is. 4 live slots ride this policy: market-watcher-offhours, news-scout-offhours, market-watcher-eod, news-scout-sentiment.

SCOPE CAVEAT (do not overstate): per the known ACCELERATE-half-inert finding (project_dynamic_workflow_cadence), cron is the FIRST gate, so a resolved 30-min interval does not make anything fire faster than its cron. The live damage is one-directional: gatherers can never be THROTTLED DOWN to 60/240 during genuinely quiet periods, because the input that would trigger throttling never varies.

EXISTING COVERAGE -- DO NOT MINT A DUPLICATE:
(1) backlog row CLEAN-PRICEANOMALY-SIGNAL-FILES-UNBOUNDED-NO-AGE-CEILING-ANYWHERE already covers the retention/age-ceiling half ('21 files live, oldest 52 days'; now 22/53d). AMEND it with this consequence -- its current framing reads as housekeeping, but the residue is corrupting an adaptive-cadence input, which is a different and higher-priority argument.
(2) archive row FIX-PRICE-ANOMALY-DISH-SIGNAL-ENVELOPE names the exact root cause ('lack from/type envelope -> skipped by drain; real anomaly:true detections reach no consumer') but its status is CANCELLED, closed 2026-07-21T18:45:38Z, next_agent=po. It was abandoned, not shipped -- verified live: both the oldest (20260702) and newest (20260824) files still have top-level keys dish_window/generated_at/schema/tickers and no envelope. That cancellation is precisely what makes the floor permanent. Reinstating it fixes new files; an age-ceiling sweep fixes the residue; BOTH are needed, and neither alone drops the gauge below 10 today (22 price_anomaly removed still leaves 8, but the floor regrows).

SECOND-ORDER, worth stating: the cancelled row also means real anomaly:true EOD detections have reached no consumer since at least 2026-07-02. That is a data-loss claim I did not verify beyond the envelope shape -- flagging, not asserting.

RECOMMEND: po amends CLEAN-PRICEANOMALY-... with this cadence consequence and decides whether to reinstate FIX-PRICE-ANOMALY-DISH-SIGNAL-ENVELOPE. Separately worth a small hardening: make the gauge count only envelope-valid files, so an undrainable file cannot masquerade as drain pressure.
